rationale:
Selected minor by explicit maintainer exception: 1.0.0 -> 1.1.0.

On 2026-09-24 the maintainer requested a minor release despite the known incompatible changes because this vault is not yet in production and their instance is disposable. This is a one-time versioning exception, not a compatibility claim or authorization to reset a database. Future releases follow the normal compatibility policy.

Assessed the complete candidate from v1.0.0 (3e24f02) through develop d1229de, including PRs #1, #2 and #3. The semantic compatibility impact is major because supported authority, HTTP/MCP and import contracts require adaptation; the maintainer explicitly chose a minor version for this pre-production release. The candidate also includes the narrowly scoped release-validation exception and its regression tests.

- HTTP (breaking): policy create/update schemas reject purpose, policy updates reject clientId, and a second policy for a client returns 409. Client responses replace policyCount with hasPolicy; disclosure reviews replace purpose with nullable statedPurpose. Read, suggestion and capture results carry typed decision reasons. Direct HTTP read/suggestion input aliases remain supported. Evidence: packages/shared/src/{policies,clients,memory-requests,memory-suggestions,common}.ts, apps/api/src/policies/policies.service.ts, docs/openapi.json and docs/api-guide.md.
- MCP (breaking): tool names/transports remain, but inputs now reject unknown keys, snake_case aliases, categories and lowercase enum values. Purpose is optional audit context; suggestedPurpose and FUNES_VAULT_SUGGESTED_PURPOSE no longer inject hints or retry requests. Each tool makes one API call. Evidence: packages/mcp/src/tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/index.test.ts and its discovery snapshot, apps/api/test/mcp-discovery.e2e.spec.ts.
- Identity/OAuth: accounts, sessions, client identities and existing OAuth grants survive migration. Login/token exchange, refresh rotation, revocation and scope names remain compatible. Consent now displays resulting app permissions; approval merges operations into the sole permission set, while refresh does not recreate removed permissions. Evidence: apps/api/src/oauth/{oauth-grants.service,oauth-permissions,oauth-consent.html}.ts, apps/api/test/oauth-permissions.e2e.spec.ts and docs/deployment-and-operations.md.
- Authority (breaking): one permission set per authenticated app replaces purpose-selected policies. Missing permissions deny before retrieval; request approvals bind policy id/version, and pre-migration approvals cannot authorize disclosure. Removed first-party permissions require explicit restoration. WRITE can permit immediate eligible proposals; capture and explicit extraction review mode remain review-only. Existing processing-consent requirements remain. Evidence: docs/adr/0044-app-permissions-and-stated-purpose.md, apps/api/src/policies/policy-evaluation.service.ts, apps/api/src/first-party-access/first-party-access.service.ts, apps/api/test/{app-permissions,disclosure-authority,oauth-permissions}.e2e.spec.ts.
- Data (breaking): only funes-vault.export.v2 imports are accepted. The upgrade migration preserves vault identities/data while dropping invalid cross-owner policies, surplus policies and policy purpose, retaining the newest valid policy deterministically. Old requests lose approval bindings; legacy CLIENT_SUGGESTION metadata is wrapped under caller, affecting old bearer-capture deduplication. Evidence: packages/shared/src/data-control.ts, packages/db/prisma/migrations/20260924000000_app_permissions/migration.sql and packages/db/scripts/test-app-permissions-migration.ts. Drain capture queues, verify a database backup, migrate with old services stopped, then start matching new images. Rollback requires restoring the pre-upgrade backup with old images; no live database reset.
- Deployment: documented runtime prerequisites, service/image names, origins and application environment variables remain unchanged; the obsolete MCP purpose hint is removed as above. Upgrade API/worker, MCP and web together after migration. Publication now requires successful exact-main-merge CI; tag pushes alone do not publish, and manual/local publishers produce SHA-only diagnostic images. Evidence: Dockerfile, Compose/env files unchanged against v1.0.0; .github/workflows/{release,publish-images}.yml, scripts/publish-images.sh, docs/releasing.md and docs/deployment-and-operations.md. Production deployment is separately authorized.
